item.title: The implied fourth wall.
item.content:encoded:
Subtlety is arguably one of the best ways to afflict the reader with a cold sense of dread. Sure, you could simply take the article at face value, then feel uneasy because there's no telling whether it predicts or creates SCPs— vastly different options that mean big trouble either way for the Foundation.

Then you realize that the general uneasiness pales in comparison to the chilling, gradual realization that this proposed SCP-001 is the perfect in-universe metaphor for the SCP Wiki, and depending on how many articles you've authored, you're the reason it's growing.

Fantastic presentation.

item.content:encoded:
On the previous page, I inquired about the identity of the author since I could not find any trace of him on this site besides this article. Now, over two years later, the author in question contacted me after having read those comments, and wishes to pass on this message.

Hi — I stumbled upon the comments on my SCP-001 proposal and have been humbled by the incredible discussion there. I saw that you posted an old comment wondering who I was and then there were a bunch of theories below that. I just thought I would take a moment to pop on and say who I was. I don't understand how this new version of the site works well enough to log in and post something (I logged in but it won't let me post or add to the discussion). I don't intend to clarify anything regarding the ambiguities in my SCP-001 proposal, but since there is confusion about authorship I thought I would just note that who I am is an author — I have five books out, the best known probably being CLOCKFIRE, a series of plays that would be impossible to produce and a kind of Lovecraft-meets-Italo Calvino thing — my main website is over at www.jonathanball.com — I thought the authorship would always be obvious and not confusing, since my name is literally on the proposal, but I guess it has been a long time! I have been keeping my eye on this site since the early days of writing this proposal but never really looked into the discussion before. Originally, I wrote this after Christian Bök — a bestselling experimental poet who created a poem-as-virus that actually was implanted into the DNA of a bacterial organism known as the XENOTEXT and is mentioned in a novel by SF author Peter Watts — told me about this SCP site he had stumbled across and spent all night reading. So that is the humble origins of this SCP-001 Proposal. Please let the other SCP-ers of the modern age know that I just read through this decade of commentary and I was greatly moved. All best wishes, Jonathan

Really nice fellow, to say the least.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
sandrewswann is rolling in his inactive membership page.

Oh, absolutely. The meta in this is leagues ahead of Swann's Proposal. The usage of meta in Swann's Proposal is almost entirely Watsonian, and the little Doylism that's there is an appeal to the emotions of the reader, equating the author (us) with gods and horror entities.

The meta here, however, represents the site itself in an abstract manner. It adds value to the work, and increases the literary value of the work. It's a metaphor for the site, and a representation of how reading the site fuels the production and writing of more articles.

Most importantly of all, the meta of JBall's 001 is subtle, but still present. The fourth wall is respected, rather than broken, but the meta is still present. This is the harder meta article to write, but it pays off well.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
After rereading this, I realize that the numerical order thing about SCP discovery is only ever implied, and not outright stated. Just because the first five SCPs were 001-002-003-004-005 doesn't necessarily mean that the sixth is 006. That alone throws the big concern that I always thought I did (and, reading the thread, a lot of people did) out the window. Those five SCPs work fine as a first five, and other SCPs could have been in nonnumerical order.

EDIT: The other interpretation — and the one presented in the excellent tale about this Pila is that SCP-001 works on something of a retrocausal basis (as seen in the tale by the inconsistent dates of recovery). That is to say, it is capable of producing objects that have always been there. This also obviates that big concern.

So, putting aside that qualm, there's something very striking to me about the nature of the current administration I see here. They seem rational and level-headed, and there's an implication of the current administration's thinking — namely, the idea of a Foundation in which the source of all anomalies has been contained, and therefore there have not been new anomalies in a while — is intriguing. It's a Foundation in control of the anomalous, and that's the Foundation I come here to read about.

Oh, and by the way, this is the best meta 001. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Why there is no answer here.
Why there is no answer here.

Argument from Completed Metaphor

The sheaf is a metaphor for this site. Therein lies the simple brilliance of the proposal, and why it stands the test of time. While all metaphors break down somewhere, and there is no non-ambiguous way to determine where that should be besides speculative argumentation, let's carry the metaphor through the mystery at the core of this proposal; does the sheaf create or report new SCPs?

Because the SCP is a metaphor for the site, it bridges the in-universe and the out-of-universe. It's not surprising then that we could have opposing conclusions based upon which perspective we choose to look at the proposal from.

The SCP identifying other SCPs in a strictly sequential fashion breaks from what we know out-of-universe about the chronological creation of SCPs on the site. Thus the most reasonable interpretation based on the metaphor from the out-of-universe perspective is to believe the sheaf is "reading" the series of SCPs, like you would on the site (starting with this proposal, by the way), and suggests it is not creating the SCPs.

In-universe, SCPs are presumably assigned numbers in a strictly stepwise fashion. So, the most reasonable conclusion to uphold from the in-universe perspective is that this SCP creates the new SCPs, as the current administration has prudently concluded. Additionally supporting this conclusion are the lines of correlative/causative suggestion given to us by the author:

At varying times following this incident, the aforementioned items were discovered.

it has been established that every event regarding the discovery of a new SCP item has followed a report on that same item appearing beneath the cover sheet of SCP-001.

The fact remains: no new SCP items appear unless SCP-001 is opened and read.

Brushing aside that the current administration is choosing the wording of these sentences and thereby coloring the only available data we have for in-universe correlation/causation (we know they already think it is causative), there is a clear indication of sequence in these sentences. The article is read and then discovered, supporting the inclination that this is a causal relationship.

So, quite cleverly, the two perspectives impinge opposing conclusions. So, the question might now be: is there really no answer?

We can reconcile both paradigms by postulating a prior causative event in-universe that results in the existence of a new in-universe SCP and its documentation in the sheaf. The out-of-universe analogy is obvious; that prior cause is us, the creators (out-of-universe, the SCP and its documentation materialize simultaneously; they are the same thing.) The reason why I choose to use this postulation as the solution to the mystery here is that it sustains the originally-intended metaphor through both the in- and out-of-universe interpretations.

So imo, in-universe, the appearance of a new SCP and its report in the sheaf are only causally related in that they are both effects of a shared cause (which leaves the in-universe generation of SCP just as mysterious as it has always been). The sure take-away is that this SCP proposal does not contain the means to come to a conclusion, only the means for a very lively discussion on the topic…and I like to think it does so intentionally.

item.title: Small suggestion
item.content:encoded:
Hi everyone. I just wanted to suggest one change to this proposal which I think may improve things. Actually thought about this a few years ago but… well, we got here eventually.

So the main thing I would suggest is to mention almost in passing that the papers had a slightly different appearance when they were viewed in the past. Perhaps 40 years ago it resembled a stack of the old dot-matrix printer paper. Some years before that, it was reported to look as though it was written on a typewriter.

The suggestion is that SCP-001 changes its appearance over time to resemble something suitable the time period, something someone may easily stumble across and read (or otherwise simply comprehend), thinking nothing of it. A printed pamphlet, a manuscript, a tapestry, a scroll, a carved tablet… a cave-painted stone.

I'm aware that such a change to the core idea requires the rest of the entry and its history to be reworked in order to fit slightly better, but I believe it would be an improvement. I think as described the exact sequence of reading about SCP-002, then 003, then 004 is a little too… neat? anyway, as others have suggested. The implication would be that reading SCP-001 simply causes another SCP to come into existence. The discovery and designation of these is really Foundation business and nothing to do with SCP-001 itself.

I do think this will diminish the proposal's sense of mystery around the cause and effect of SCP-001 somewhat, so if that's the thing you like the most about it, maybe this idea isn't doing much for you. That's fair enough. To me, I think the benefits outweigh that loss but I definitely feel it.

Perhaps before time & space there was only SCP-001. And, slowly, something came to comprehend it. And here we are. (Enjoying the phrase 'in the beginning was the word & the word was with god & the word was god' in this context)

Anyway, that's about it. Thanks.
